lessons.title: AI and work: exposure is not a forecast
lessons.subtitle: What OECD and IAB figures say, and what they don't

sections.title: What a jobs figure measures
sections.content:
Figures on threatened jobs measure different things:

1. Task exposure: a technology overlaps with an occupation's tasks.
2. Technical substitution potential: tasks could be automated with today's technology.
3. Adoption: an employer introduces the technology and rebuilds the workflow.
4. Employment effect: working time, headcount, wages or skill requirements change.

Frey and Osborne estimated a theoretical automation probability for US occupations in 2013. With different data and methods, the OECD Employment Outlook 2023 reports the employment share in high-risk occupations across the OECD countries studied, with no forecast for Germany or for job losses.

The IAB uses BERUFENET to work out what share of an occupation's core tasks available technology could in principle perform fully automatically, and states that substitutability does not mean the task gets automated.

Sources: OECD Employment Outlook 2023, Chapter 3; IAB Brief Report 5/2024 on the 2022 recalculation.

sections.title: What "better than people" means
sections.content:
"AI is better than people" says nothing without test conditions. Check:

- Task: are input, output and quality measure defined?
- Data: do the test data match the real population and later deployment?
- Consequences: what does an error cost, and who reviews borderline cases?
- Environment: standardised, or shifting physically and socially?

A model can ace a narrow image-classification test and be unfit for the clinic. A language model can speed up a draft and invent facts in it; a planning system can handle every standard case and fail on one rare exception.

Even when the system scores better, people and organisations keep legal responsibility, approvals and the weighing of interests.

sections.title: When one task becomes automatable
sections.content:
An occupation is a bundle of tasks. When one becomes automatable, the employer can save time, handle more cases, redistribute work, raise quality or cut jobs. Demand, cost, liability, co-determination and new tasks play a part too.

Whether radiology software that flags anomalies in images saves work or adds review turns on hit and error rates, the patient population, integration and required oversight. Diagnosis and treatment stay medical work.

For your own job, a task analysis helps more than any forecast: which steps are standardised, where do errors arise, which decisions need expertise, context or approval, and where does the tool add checking?

quiz.questionText: Which statement about labour-market studies on AI and automation is correct?

answerOptions.text: Every exposure figure directly forecasts future job losses
Exposure, technical potential and employment effect are different measures
The IAB measures only AI already in use in companies
The OECD Employment Outlook 2023 forecasts German unemployment caused by AI

quiz.explanation: Exposure and substitution potential show possible overlaps. Adoption and the employment effect also turn on economic, legal and organisational factors.

quiz.questionText: What does the IAB substitution potential based on BERUFENET measure?

answerOptions.text: How many employees already use generative AI
Which occupations disappear within a year
What share of core tasks technology could in principle perform fully automatically
Which companies must automate by law

quiz.explanation: It measures technical potential. Actual adoption, viability and future job losses are not in the figure.

quiz.questionText: What follows from an automatable sub-task?

answerOptions.text: The whole occupation disappears within the next planning horizon
The technology is economical in every organisation
Every remaining task becomes more valuable to employees
The workflow can change; the employment effect needs separate examination

quiz.explanation: The deployment in the organisation decides whether technical potential becomes time saved, extra review, more cases or fewer positions.

lessons.title: AI as assistance: measure the benefit yourself
lessons.subtitle: Who checks, who approves, which data go in

sections.title: Assistance without a performance promise
sections.content:
An assisted workflow gives the system one bounded step; approval and accountability stay with a named person. You measure in your own process whether it saves time.

Three invented examples:
- A nurse drafts from approved, data-protection-compliant notes and checks every statement against the record. Patient data belong only in a system approved for them.
- An accountant has unusual entries flagged. The flag means: look closer. It does not establish fraud or an error.
- A communications team generates image drafts and checks them for rights, factual fit, disclosure and approval before publishing.

A controlled test fixes task, permitted data, quality criteria, reviewer, stopping point and logging in advance. Only its measurements show the benefit.

sections.title: What AI literacy covers
sections.content:
To approve an AI draft you need five abilities, and programming is not one of them:

1. Describe the task: purpose, context, format, limits.
2. Review the output: check claims, figures and sources against reliable material.
3. Recognise risk: stop at personal data, confidential information or consequential decisions and involve the responsible function.
4. Place the tool: approval status, data handling, limits, version changes.
5. Record the work: where the process demands it, keep inputs, relevant outputs, changes and approvals.

Article 4 of the AI Act, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, requires providers and deployers to take measures that support the development of AI literacy among their staff and others acting on their behalf. It does not demand a guaranteed level per person.

sections.title: When the works council has a say
sections.content:
A tool counts how fast a colleague closes her tickets. Absent a statutory or collective-agreement rule, Section 87(1)(6) of the German Works Constitution Act (BetrVG) gives the works council co-determination over introducing and using technical equipment intended to monitor employees' behaviour or performance.

Function and use decide whether an AI system is covered. The right belongs to the works council, not to each employee.

Raise these points in your organisation:
- purpose and supported decision
- employee data collected, inferred or stored
- who sees the analyses and how long they are stored
- human oversight, correction and complaint route
- training and binding rules of use

If employer and works council cannot agree in a co-determination matter, the conciliation committee decides under Section 87(2). Whether your system is covered needs qualified employment-law analysis.

quiz.questionText: How do you recognise a controlled assistance workflow?

answerOptions.text: A fluent output counts as correct without further review
Task, permitted data, review and accountable approval are fixed in advance
Personal data may go into any available system
The benefit is taken from general vendor claims

quiz.explanation: A bounded task, protected data, quality criteria and accountable approval make the benefit measurable in your own process.

quiz.questionText: Which ability belongs to AI literacy if you have never programmed?

answerOptions.text: Training and calibrating your own models
Writing Python code for AI applications
Configuring and maintaining AI hardware
Assessing AI output critically and seeing its limits

quiz.explanation: AI literacy means checking output and knowing its limits. Programming is no prerequisite.

quiz.questionText: Which rule can bite for an AI system meant to monitor employee behaviour or performance?

answerOptions.text: Article 4 AI Act (measures supporting AI literacy)
Section 106 GewO (employer's right to issue instructions)
Article 22 GDPR (automated individual decisions)
Section 87(1)(6) BetrVG (co-determination for technical monitoring equipment)

quiz.explanation: The rule covers technical equipment intended to monitor behaviour or performance. Whether it applies turns on the system and its deployment.

lessons.title: Which tasks can change, and what you check yourself
lessons.subtitle: Which task characteristics count

sections.title: Where technical potential runs high
sections.content:
The technical potential tends to be high when a step repeats daily, has digital inputs, follows clear rules or a quality measure and takes place in a physical setting that barely changes. Examples are transferring structured data, checking formal completeness and drafting from a template.

Adoption stays open: bad data, rare exceptions, liability, integration cost or follow-up checks can eat the benefit. The other way round, technology can support single steps in almost any job.

The IAB sorts core tasks within occupations against market-ready technology and refreshes that snapshot regularly.

sections.title: What makes automation hard
sections.content:
Automation gets hard when a task combines several of the following traits, as on an unfamiliar building site or in care with patchy information and a relative in the room:

- a changing physical setting and fine-motor work
- incomplete information and rare exceptions
- direct responsibility for safety or fundamental rights
- negotiation among several parties
- relationship, trust or local knowledge

None of that makes an occupation "AI-proof". Documentation, planning and retrieval can shift in care, trades, teaching and advice too, and robotics can move physical tasks over time. So look at single tasks.

sections.title: What you can do yourself
sections.content:
1. Inventory your tasks: write down recurring steps, error consequences, data needed and approvals.
2. Test safely: approved tools and test data only, nothing confidential or personal, compared against a reference fixed in advance.
3. Get advice: Germany's Federal Employment Agency offers "Berufsberatung im Erwerbsleben", career guidance for people in employment, with information on training and funding.
4. Ask in your organisation: your manager, data protection, information security and any works council.

Article 5 of the AI Act has banned certain practices since 2 February 2025, among them emotion recognition at work, exceptions aside. Recruitment and selection systems can fall under Annex III; for stand-alone Annex III systems the high-risk rules apply from 2 December 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. The AGG, GDPR and employment law can apply today.

If your application runs through such a system, ask about purpose, data, the meaning of the output, human involvement and accountability.

quiz.questionText: Which task typically carries the higher technical automation potential?

answerOptions.text: A negotiation among several parties in a new conflict
A repair in an unfamiliar physical environment
A repeated formal completeness check on structured digital data
A consequential single-case judgement on incomplete information

quiz.explanation: Repeated digital steps that can be checked clearly often carry the higher technical potential. Whether an employer automates them stays open.

quiz.questionText: What does Germany's Federal Employment Agency offer employees with training questions?

answerOptions.text: Automatic retraining for every occupation touched by AI
Career guidance for people in employment, with information on training and funding
A guarantee that every course you want gets funded
Mandatory certification under Article 4 of the AI Act

quiz.explanation: The guidance covers training and funding. Whether a measure is funded turns on you, the measure and the rules in force.

quiz.questionText: Which statement about the EU AI Act at work is correct?

answerOptions.text: Article 5 prohibits every form of recruitment AI
All high-risk obligations have applied since 2 February 2025
Article 5 has nothing to do with the workplace
Since 2 February 2025, Article 5 has banned certain practices at work

quiz.explanation: Article 5 bans precisely named practices such as emotion recognition at work, exceptions aside. Check hiring systems separately under Annex III, the AGG, GDPR and co-determination.
